rubric_hint.basis: prompts/rubric.md v1 applied to all rings 0-1000 m and effort; a default, not a verdict

reasons.claim: Nine eligible species are recorded beyond 250 m but within 1000 m, and none within 250 m. They include two EN lichens: Megalaria laureri (859 m, 2024) and Bellicidia incompta (904 m). They also include VU lichens and fungi, for example Calicium quercinum (606 m), Gyalecta carneola (621 m, 13 records) and Hydnellum fagiscabrosum (914 m). Lack of continuity forest is among the threats listed for all of them.
Within 250 m there are no eligible species. Two site-bound NT fungi are recorded there (Fistulina hepatica at 197 m, Grifola frondosa at 209 m), which is fewer than the 3 needed for the NT rule.
Effort is adequate (1908 records within 1000 m, 97th percentile). 143 records are kept within 250 m and none lie inside the polygon.
Only 1.5% of the polygon overlaps 2005 and 2007 completed fellings, so it is not already felled.

uncertainties: 99 coarse records within 250 m were dropped for uncertainty, which could hide eligible records near the site.
The nearest eligible records are 606 m or more from the polygon. Their relevance to the stand in the polygon is not established.
The notification lists 0 ha natfor_ha against a 6.34 ha polygon. What this field means for the habitat is not stated in the evidence.
Records show a species was recorded, not that it occupies the polygon today.
not_established: Whether any red-listed species occurs in the polygon.
The stand's age, structure or habitat quality.
That the site is safe to fell.
next_action: A reviewer should check the stand's tree species, age and continuity-forest features. The reviewer should also check whether it is connected to the habitat of the lichen and fungus records 600-900 m away, and look at the dropped coarse records.
